## Natural history notes

A tiny grass-veneer moth characterized by narrow clay-colored to pale tan wings, a slender body, and a simple grass-like resting posture that helps it blend into dry stems and litter. In Florida, the Diminutive Grass-Veneer is likely found in open grassy habitats such as pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, marsh edges, lawns, pastures, and wet prairies where grasses and sedges are abundant. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed among grasses or near the bases of stems, supporting birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
